claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford: The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday it had removed the B1 bombers from the base in England back to their home stations in America.
- France braces for national day of school protests after injuries and mass arrests: France prepares for a day of protests in support of students who’ve been demanding more investment in education.
- Saudi Arabia urged to spare man sentenced to death over Facebook post: Anojan Sivarasa faces execution after he was found guilty of blasphemy over a Facebook comment.
- Separatist party projected to win Quebec election, adding new test to Canada's unity: The Parti Québécois, which secured a minority, has vowed to hold an independence referendum in the years to come.
- Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?: The city's space boom raises questions about the role of the state in backing important industries.
- Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway: Saudi-backed forces gave conflicting reports of whether they had also seized the port city of Mokha, near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
- Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two: Nidal Malik Hasan killed 13 unarmed US soldiers and injured another 32 and his execution will be the first by the US military since 1961.
- UK MPs call for investigation after Lutnick-Epstein whistleblower dies: Simon Andriesz said he felt let down by the UK's Financial Conduct Authority before his death last month.
- Watch: Moment Indonesian sneaker shop is torn apart by explosion: Police have said it is “strongly suspected” that the incident was caused by a gas leak.
- 'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa: For many locals on this island, the arrest has brought decades of frustration back to the fore.
- Trump says he will stop using taxpayer funds for ads after bipartisan pushback: The ads, which tout Trump and his policies, could have violated US laws barring public government funds being spent on political advertising.
- Samoa leader apologises for Nazi salute after video from 2007 emerges: Schmidt acknowledged that his actions "were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt".
